title: How Bestseller Turned Fragmented Workforce Data into Trusted People Intelligence
summary: Bestseller uses SAP SuccessFactors HCM and People Intelligence to replace fragmented workforce data with a single governed foundation.
body_markdown:
Bestseller uses SAP SuccessFactors HCM and People Intelligence in SAP Business Data Cloud to replace fragmented, inconsistent workforce data with a single governed foundation, so leaders across all brands and countries work from the same numbers and focus on decisions.


When Kristoffer Buur joined[Bestseller](https://bestseller.com/) ’s people organization more than 10 years ago, the company was already a global fashion group with a broad portfolio of brands and stores. Today it counts more than[50 fashion brands](https://bestseller.com/brands) and about 30,000 colleagues in around 45 countries. Its products are sold in about 2,800 branded chain stores and roughly 16,000 multi-brand and department stores across the world. Back then, it lacked a reliable answer to the most basic workforce question: how many people actually work here?


“We believed our headcount was around 12,000,” says Buur, who leads Global HR and People Technology Initiatives at the Danish fashion group. “When we brought everything together, the real number was closer to 20,000.”


No data had been falsified. No system had failed. The number was simply scattered across multiple systems, each counting differently. And that gap, nearly 8,000 people, is exactly what happens when a large, fast-growing organization runs on fragmented people data.

## **The real problem wasn’t the data. It was trust.**


Bestseller’s challenge was not unique. HR teams at complex, multi-country organizations frequently find that the same metric—headcount, termination rate, open positions—produces a different answer depending on which system or team you ask.


The consequence is predictable. Meetings that should focus on what to do next become debates about which figure is correct. Leaders stop relying on the data. HR reverts to producing reports rather than enabling decisions.


Buur puts it plainly: “If two leaders look at the same question and reach two different answers, the meeting becomes a decision about the numbers, not about what to do.”


Before Bestseller could use data to act, it needed data it could trust.


## **Foundation first**


“Everyone wants to talk about AI and prediction models. I understand why,” Buur says. “But it’s a bit like building a house. Most organizations want to start with the roof. We chose to start with the foundation.” That foundation is SAP SuccessFactors HCM, which Bestseller calls its “people system.” It now holds the full, clean employee lifecycle across every brand and country.


On top of it, Bestseller uses[People Intelligence in SAP Business Data Cloud](https://www.sap.com/products/hcm/data-cloud.html) . This is where governance meets business context: definitions, rules, and retail-specific logic, such as store managers, weekly working hours, and location hierarchies, are encoded once and applied everywhere.


The result is a three-layer architecture that moves from raw data to decision support:


- **People system:**[SAP SuccessFactors HCM](https://www.sap.com/products/hcm.html) as the trusted source of workforce data
- **People Intelligence:** the analytics layer, with governance definitions and Bestseller-specific business context
- **Decision layer:** role-based views shaped for the leaders who use them, across countries, brands, and functions


## **What leaders see today**


Every leader’s view brings the same perspectives together on one page: headcount, working hours, hires, terminations, and open positions. Each is compared to the previous month and the previous year, so leaders can see which direction they are moving in. Growth in stores and teams is visible across countries, brands, and functions, all from the same foundation.


In recruiting, Bestseller’s business is seasonal, and that rhythm is now visible before it arrives. “Our leaders could see those peaks coming and plan for them instead of explaining them afterwards,” Buur says.


Turnover is where the impact has been most significant. “We employ many young people, so of course we expect movement,” Buur says. “But there is a big difference between saying we have high turnover because we employ young people and actually seeing where and why.”


The early leavers view tracks terminations among employees with less than three, three to six, and six to nine months of tenure. Voluntary and involuntary terminations are shown alongside. A color-coded termination rate for every country means a leader can spot an issue in seconds.


## **The same numbers, everywhere**


What makes the views meaningful is not what they show, but what sits underneath them. When a country’s HR team talks to headquarters about headcount or turnover, both sides are using the same definitions, the same rules, the same system.


Some markets have grown their headcount by a third or more in a single year, while their open positions have fallen sharply. Elsewhere, a single month’s hiring push, with many new hires and only a handful of leavers, is immediately visible. The early-leaver view then answers the follow-up question automatically: are those new hires staying?


Each type of leader sees a view shaped for their context. A retail leader sees store staffing, working hours, and hiring across the chain. A country leader sees growth, vacancies, and turnover in their market. A brand leader sees the workforce behind the brand across countries. The views differ, but the foundation and the governance are the same.


## **What changed**


The shift Buur describes is concrete. Before People Intelligence, meetings started with “Which number is correct?” and HR produced reports for most of them. Turnover was explained after it had already happened.


Now the question is “What actions do we take?” Leaders spot patterns before they become problems. Data quality errors surface quickly, because leaders who trust the numbers do not want to be caught presenting incorrect ones, so they flag and fix them.


“Instead of debating which number is correct, our leaders focus on what to do,” Buur says. “That’s the change.”


Buur sums it up: “People Intelligence helped Bestseller make faster, more informed decisions by combining three things: trusted workforce data, governance, and role-specific leadership insights. If you put those together, you turn data into actionable business outcomes. For us, the journey goes from knowing what happened to understanding why, and step by step towards action before it happens.”

## **Partnership matters**


Bestseller was among the early customers working with People Intelligence. Buur credits two partners with making it work:[SAP Consulting](https://www.sap.com/services-support) , who brought product expertise, and[Effective People](https://www.sap.com/partners/profile/effective-people) , who knew the SAP SuccessFactors landscape and Bestseller’s data.


“Instead of three parties speaking three different languages, we built one team that understands the business, the data, and the technology,” Buur says. “That’s what turned our wishes into something concrete.”


## **What comes next**


People Intelligence at Bestseller is not a finished project. The company is building an absence report on the same foundation and plans to expand the coverage of report types. Each addition strengthens the data layer and moves the organization closer to acting before issues occur, rather than responding after them.


“This isn’t really about dashboards,” Buur says. “It’s about turning people’s data into insights, insights into actions, and actions into better decisions.”


The headcount question that once produced two very different answers, 12,000 or 20,000, now has one.
